id_and_class.summary: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz holds that reality is made of monads, simple immaterial substances whose whole inner life is perception and appetition. Perception is everywhere in nature, but consciousness (which he calls apperception) is a rarer, reflective grade of perception: a perception of one's own perceptions. Mind and body never interact; God set their series in agreement from the start.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Reflective Perception in Simple Substances

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is apperception, the reflective knowledge of a monad's own perceptual states. Perception itself, the representation of many things within one simple unity, belongs to every monad.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: No causal interaction. Each monad unfolds its perceptions from within, and its body is a correlated mirror kept in step by pre-established harmony, like clocks set once to run together. Extended matter is a well-founded phenomenon, an appearance of aggregates of monads.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (perception is a basic property of every monad; consciousness is a higher grade of it, not something produced by arranging matter)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Each monad represents the whole universe from its own point of view, which makes it a perpetual living mirror of the cosmos. Representation is a basic feature of reality, and subjectivity is the unique perspective of each simple substance.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Experience is the internal, self-generated unfolding of a simple substance. The mill argument holds that no arrangement of parts pushing one another can explain perception, so its felt unity must belong to a simple subject.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Infinitely many simple, non-spatial monads with perception and appetition; God, who chose the best possible world and created its monads in harmony; matter as a well-founded appearance.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Reflection gives minds access to their own perceptions, though most perceptions are too faint to notice. Leibniz's case rests on rational argument from the requirement that true being needs true unity.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: A continuous hierarchy by distinctness of perception: bare monads with confused, unconscious perceptions; animal souls with sensation and memory; rational minds with reflection, self-consciousness and knowledge of necessary truths.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Perception, unconscious mental life, sensation, self-consciousness, the unity of experience, and moral personhood.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The split between perception and apperception: a state becomes conscious when it is reflectively known, which some commentators (Gennaro) read as an early higher-order theory.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Appetition, the internal striving of a monad, carries it from one perception to the next. Apperception comes and goes; it is not given to all souls nor at all times to any one soul.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Perception pervades all of nature. Sensation is found in animals and reflective consciousness in rational minds, so consciousness is graded and distributed rather than confined to humans.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Monads are windowless, so nothing acts on them from outside. Apperception has a moral function: reflection lets a mind know God and join the City of God, making it eligible for justice, mercy and reward.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: A perception represents a manifold within one partless subject, so unity is given by the simplicity of the monad. Conscious experience is never assembled from material parts.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Petites perceptions, minute insensible perceptions, are always present and causally effective. We hear the roar of the sea because we unconsciously perceive the sound of each wave.
core_claims_and_evidence: Leibniz argues that extended matter is divisible without limit, so true substances must be simple, partless monads.
The mill argument holds that walking inside a perceiving machine would reveal only parts pushing one another, nothing that explains perception.
Perception is distinct from consciousness, and most of mental life consists of unnoticed petites perceptions, against Descartes's view that all thought is conscious.
Animals genuinely feel through sensation, while only rational minds have reflective self-consciousness.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical and theological: rationalist metaphysics, a priori argument, and the principles of sufficient reason and the best possible world.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Pre-established harmony depends on a divine act and cannot be secularized; without it, windowless monads leave each inner life unrelated to anything else. Placing Leibniz among neutral monists strains the fit, since his basic entities are mental and there are infinitely many of them.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Leibniz does not offer a theory of consciousness in the neuroscientific sense. The account says nothing about how brain processes correlate with apperception beyond divine coordination.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Internally consistent within its theistic rationalism. It is a third option between Cartesian dualism and mechanistic materialism, structurally close to dual-aspect views because the mental and bodily series correspond exactly without interacting.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Since the mill argument holds that no mechanism of parts can perceive, a machine considered as an aggregate cannot be conscious.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Monads can begin and end only by divine creation and annihilation, and minds are members of the City of God, which follows from the view that souls are simple substances.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: God chose this world as the best possible and stands to minds as a prince to his subjects, so reflective consciousness has a moral and divine purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: Consciousness belongs to a simple substance and cannot be produced by any arrangement of parts, so a simulation could not carry it.
